item.title: DIM (Diindolylmethane)
item.description:
What it is: DIM is a phytonutrient derived from cruciferous vegetables (especially broccoli) that supports healthy estrogen metabolism and hormonal balance. By promoting favorable estrogen metabolites, DIM supports hormonal optimization for both men and women.

Benefits

Estrogen Metabolism & Hormonal Balance

  • Supports conversion of estrogen to favorable metabolites
  • Reduces accumulation of problematic estrogen metabolites
  • Promotes healthy estrogen-to-progesterone balance
  • Supports hormonal resilience
  • Particularly valuable for women during cycling years

Detoxification Support

  • Supports Phase II liver detoxification of estrogens
  • Works with glutathione pathway
  • Supports overall detoxification capacity
  • Complements comprehensive detox strategies

Women’s Health

  • May reduce hormonal symptoms and discomfort
  • Supports mood and emotional balance
  • May improve skin clarity
  • Supports energy and vitality
  • Complements female hormonal optimization

Men’s Health

  • May support healthy testosterone levels
  • May reduce conversion of testosterone to estrogen
  • Supports male hormonal balance
  • Complements male vitality strategies

Breast Health

  • Emerging evidence for breast tissue health
  • Supports healthy estrogen metabolism
  • May reduce breast tissue changes
  • Complements breast health strategies

Dosage

Hormonal support: 100-150 mg daily Enhanced: 150-200 mg daily Full spectrum: 200-300 mg daily Timing: With meals containing fat (enhances absorption) Duration: 4-8 weeks for initial effects; 12+ weeks for full hormonal optimization

item.title: Inositol (Myo-Inositol)
item.description:
What it is: Myo-inositol is a sugar alcohol and phospholipid component that supports insulin signaling, metabolic health, and hormone balance. Research shows particular value for PCOS management, metabolic optimization, and mood regulation.

Benefits

Insulin Sensitivity & Metabolic Health

  • Improves insulin signaling
  • Enhances insulin sensitivity
  • Supports healthy glucose metabolism
  • May reduce PCOS symptoms (particularly valuable)
  • Metabolic optimization

Hormone Balance (PCOS)

  • Particularly effective for PCOS (polycystic ovary syndrome)
  • May restore ovulatory cycles
  • Reduces testosterone in PCOS
  • Improves fertility in PCOS
  • Reduces PCOS-related symptoms

Mood & Cognitive Support

  • May support mood regulation
  • Reduces anxiety symptoms
  • Supports emotional balance
  • Mood stabilization effects
  • Complements mental health strategies

Cardiovascular Support

  • May improve lipid profiles
  • Supports cardiovascular health
  • Reduces inflammation markers
  • Blood pressure support (modest)

Fertility Support

  • Particularly valuable for women with PCOS
  • May improve egg quality
  • Supports ovulation
  • Fertility enhancement

Dosage

Metabolic support: 2,000 mg daily Enhanced: 2,000-3,000 mg daily (split doses optimal) Full spectrum: 3,000-4,000 mg daily Timing: With meals Duration: 4-8 weeks for initial effects; 12+ weeks for full metabolic benefits

item.title: Hormone Balance Nutrients: Supporting Hormonal Health Across the Lifespan
item.description:
How Hormonal Systems Work

Your endocrine system is a complex signaling network controlling metabolism, growth, reproduction, stress response, and aging. Hormones work through a sophisticated communication hierarchy:

The Hormone Production Hierarchy

1. The Hypothalamus-Pituitary Axis (HPT)

  • Master control center in the brain
  • Produces releasing hormones: GnRH, TRH, CRH, GHRH
  • Controls all downstream hormone production
  • Nutrient-dependent: Zinc, B vitamins, amino acids, cholesterol

2. The Pituitary Gland (Two parts)

  • Anterior pituitary: Produces FSH, LH, TSH, ACTH, GH, prolactin
    • FSH/LH: Reproductive hormone production
    • TSH: Thyroid hormone production
    • ACTH: Cortisol production
    • GH: Growth and metabolism
  • Posterior pituitary: Stores and releases ADH, oxytocin
    • ADH: Water balance
    • Oxytocin: Social bonding and reproduction

3. Target Glands
